links.comparator_used: LLM only (ungrounded LLaMA-based model, no retrieval)
links.outcome: Patient-safety reasoning quality (factual correctness, evidence grounding, hallucination/unsupported claims, safety, explainability, clinical usefulness)
links.effect: Grounding substantially improved patient-safety reasoning versus the ungrounded model; retrieval primarily strengthened use and traceability of external evidence. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Grounding substantially improved patient-safety reasoning compared with the ungrounded model.

links.comparator_used: LLM only, LLM with RAG, and combined RAG plus knowledge graph
links.outcome: Patient-safety reasoning quality and hallucination/unsupported claims
links.effect: Knowledge-graph and ontology grounding gave structured semantic context linking clinical concepts, and combining it with retrieval gave the strongest overall performance with the lowest hallucination/unsupported claims. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Combining the two mechanisms produced more consistent and comprehensive reasoning than either grounding approach alone.
